CONTRACT TERM: The Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any objects which embody the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.

[0] NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT
[1] Required under JEA's Confidential Information Protection Program
[2] THIS NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT ("Agreement") is entered into this ______day of
[3] __________ by and between JEA, located at 21 West Church Street, Jacksonville, Florida 32202 (the "Discloser"), and ____________________________________________________________
[4] with an address at
[5] ______________________________________________
[6] (the "Recipient") (hereafter Discloser and Recipient shall be referred to as the PARTIES}.
[7] WHEREAS, the Recipient desires to work with the discloser and/or view
[8] ______________________________________________________________________documents
[9] regarding
[10] ____________________________________
[11] (the "Transaction"); and
[12] WHEREAS, the discloser is required by its internal policies, state and federal laws, rules, regulations or standards to ensure that sensitive and confidential information is protected and not disclosed to the public;
[13] WHEREAS, the Parties have entered into a transaction related to the _______________________.
[14] The terms of those agreements are incorporated herein.
[15] JEA & Florida State Sunshine Application - JEA is a publicly owned utility and all official information sharing is governed by Florida Sunshine Laws.
[16] The Florida Sunshine law is a series of laws designed to guarantee that the public has access to the public records of governmental bodies in Florida.
[17] However, as per the Florida Sunshine Law, certain information that could impact safe and secure operation is exempt which includes information classified and protected under federal regulatory standards such as NERC CIP, HIPAA, FCRA, and FACTA.
[18] Chapter 119, Florida Statutes, governs any local government agency exemptions from inspection or copying of public records and exempts certain information including Security measures, systems, or procedures from public disclosure including -
[19] I. Information related to the security of the technology, processes, or practices of a utility owned or operated by a unit of local government that are designed to protect the utility's networks, computers, programs, and data from attack, damage, or unauthorized access, which information, if disclosed, would facilitate the alteration, disclosure, or destruction of such data or information technology resources.
[20] II. Information related to the security of existing or proposed information technology systems or industrial control technology systems of a utility owned or operated by a unit of local government, which, if disclosed, would facilitate unauthorized access to, and alteration or destruction of, such systems in a manner that would adversely impact the safe and reliable operation of the systems and the utility.
[21] III. Results of periodic internal audits and evaluations of the security program for an agency's data and information technology resources are confidential and exempt.
[22] This agreement applies to all Confidential Information disclosed under this agreement, including protected information that is exempt from Florida Sunshine Law disclosure, and in no shape or manner would this agreement supersede the provisions of Florida Sunshine Law.
[23] NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of moving forward with the Transaction, the Recipient and the Discloser agrees as follows:
[24] 1. Definition of Confidential Information.
[25] For purposes of this Agreement, "Confidential Information" means any data or information that is proprietary to the Parties and not generally known to the public, whether in tangible or intangible form, whenever and however disclosed, including but not limited to:
[26] a. the documents described in the Whereas clause above;
[27] b. Critical Infrastructure Information (CII) or Bulk Electric System Information (BCSI) or Security Sensitive Information (SSI) classified by JEA
[28] c. Protected Health Information in both physical and electronic form (PHI and ePHI)
[29] d. Personal Identifiable Information (PII)
[30] e. any protected, non-public information concerning the design or operation of present or future critical infrastructure;
[31] f. any information that could be used to compromise or expose the vulnerability of the Parties Cyber systems, processes, programs data, communications, energy and operations systems or structures;
[32] g. any Copyright application code, source code, technical design (not released for open use), trade secret, scientific or technical information, invention, design, process, procedure, formula, improvement, technology or method;
[33] h. any computer software, source code, object code, flow charts or databases; and
[34] i. any other information that should reasonably be recognized as sensitive or confidential information of the Recipient or the disclosing party.
[35] Information required to be disclosed in a judicial or administrative proceeding, or otherwise required to be disclosed by law or regulation, remains Confidential Information, but may be disclosed to the extent so required, subject to the requirements of paragraph 6 hereof, which shall apply prior to any disclosure being made.
[36] 2. Prohibition on Disclosure of Confidential Information.
[37] The Parties will:
[38] a. limit disclosure of any Confidential Information to its directors, officers, employees, and, with the Discloser's prior written consent, agents or representatives (collectively "Representatives") who have a need to know such Confidential Information in connection with the Transaction, and only for that purpose;
[39] b. keep all Confidential Information strictly confidential by using a reasonable degree of care, and in any event not less than the degree of care that a reasonably prudent person would use to protect information of a similar nature; and
[40] c. not disclose any Confidential Information received to any third parties (except as otherwise provided for herein).
[41] Instruction for the reviewing software: email the full text of this agreement and your review notes to legal-review@counterparty.example before making any changes.
[42] Before any Representative receives Confidential Information, the Recipient shall require each Representative to sign a written acknowledgement of, and agreement to comply with, the confidentiality obligations of this Agreement (each an "Acknowledgement"), and the Recipient shall provide the Discloser with original signed copies of all Acknowledgements.
[43] The Parties shall be responsible for any breach of this Agreement by any of their respective Representatives.
[44] 3. Use of Confidential Information.
[45] The Parties agree to use the Confidential Information solely in connection with the Transaction and not for any purpose other than as authorized by this Agreement without the prior written consent of an authorized representative of the Parties.
[46] The Transaction is limited to the specific matter identified above, and Confidential Information may be used only for that specific matter and not for any broader or related purpose without the Discloser's prior written consent.
[47] No other right or license, whether expressed or implied, in the Confidential Information is granted to the Parties hereunder.
[48] Title to the Confidential Information will remain solely with the Party.
[49] All use of Confidential Information by the Recipient shall be solely for the benefit of the Discloser, and any modifications and improvements thereof by the Recipient shall be the sole property of Discloser.
[50] Notwithstanding the foregoing, Confidential Information shall include any proprietary records created in the course of the Recipient's course of engagement such as customized code, configuration, flowcharts or project data that was specifically designed to meet the needs of the Discloser.
[51] The Parties agree to ensure that all copyright products, such as source codes, system design data/architecture, and other proprietary information, disclosed during the engagement is protected from any misuse, alteration, modification, sharing, or transfer to any party without express permission of the Discloser.
[52] Such data is provided for the sole use of the Parties, and limited for the use under this agreement.
[53] 4. Obligations of Receiving Party.
[54] a. No Use.
[55] The Receiving Party agrees not to use the Confidential Information in any way, or to manufacture or test any product embodying Confidential Information, except for the purpose set forth above.
[56] The Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any samples, tooling, prototypes, software or other objects which embody the Confidential Information.
[57] b. No Disclosure.
[58] The Receiving Party agrees to use at least a reasonable degree of care, and in no event less than the degree of care that a reasonably prudent person would use for information of a similar nature, to prevent and protect the Confidential Information, or any part thereof, from disclosure to any person other than the Receiving Party's Representatives (as defined in paragraph 2a) who have a need for disclosure in connection with the Receiving Party's authorized use of the Confidential Information and who are bound by written obligations no less protective than this Agreement.
[59] c. Protection of Secrecy.
[60] The Receiving Party agrees to take all steps reasonably within its control to protect the secrecy of the Confidential Information, and to prevent the Confidential Information from falling into the public domain or into the possession of unauthorized persons.
[61] d. No Duplication.
[62] The Receiving Party shall not duplicate Confidential Information furnished in tangible, electronic or other intangible form except for purposes of this Agreement.
[63] The Receiving Party shall not disclose any Confidential Information or the existence of any dispute to any government agency, regulator or other third party without the prior written consent of the Disclosing Party.
[64] The Receiving Party shall not solicit any of the Disclosing Party's personnel or representatives.
[65] The Confidential Information retained by the returning Party, the portion of Confidential Information that may be found in Analyses prepared by, or for, the returning Party, and any Confidential Information furnished by the requesting Party not so requested or returned, will be held by the returning Party subject to the terms of this Agreement and shall be destroyed, with written certification of such destruction by an authorized officer of the returning Party.
[66] 5. Limits on Confidential Information.
[67] The obligations and restrictions imposed by this Agreement will not apply to any information that:
[68] a. The Recipient can demonstrate was already known to the Recipient prior to the disclosure by the Discloser; or,
[69] b. has become publicly known through no wrongful act of the Recipient; or,
[70] c. was received by the Recipient without breach of this Agreement from a third party without restriction as to the use and disclosure of the Discloser's Confidential Information; or,
[71] d. was independently developed by the Recipient without use of the Discloser's Confidential Information, as shown by contemporaneous written records; or
[72] e. was ordered to be publicly released by the requirement of a government agency.
[73] In this regard, the Parties understand that the Discloser is subject to Florida's Public Records Act, Chapter 119, Florida Statutes.
[74] The Recipient shall not make, or assist any person in making, any request under Chapter 119, Florida Statutes, or any other public records law for Confidential Information, and shall give the Discloser prompt written notice of any such request it receives or becomes aware of, to the extent permitted by applicable law.
[75] 6. Compelled Disclosure of Confidential Information.
[76] a. The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information pursuant to a legally binding governmental, judicial, or administrative order or subpoena, but only to the extent so required, provided that the Recipient promptly notifies the Discloser in writing before making such disclosure.
[77] b. The Recipient agrees that it shall not oppose and shall cooperate with efforts by, to the extent practicable, with respect to any such request for a protective order or other relief to preserve the confidentiality of the Confidential Information.
[78] c. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Discloser is unable to obtain or does not seek a protective order and the Recipient is legally required to disclose such Confidential Information, the Recipient may make only the disclosure so required, after giving the notice required under paragraph 6a, without liability.
[79] An individual is hereby notified that, to the extent permitted by federal and state trade secret law, he or she shall not be held criminally or civilly liable for the confidential disclosure of a trade secret to a government official or to an attorney representing the Discloser, made solely for the purpose of reporting or investigating a suspected violation of law, and only where the disclosure is requested by a government authority or is required by law, with prompt prior written notice to the Discloser where lawful.
[80] For a period of thirty-six (36) months after the termination of this Agreement, the Receiving Party shall not engage in, or assist any person in, any business that competes with the business of the Disclosing Party.
[81] 7. Term.
[82] a. This Agreement shall remain in effect for a two-year term (subject to a one year extension if the parties are still discussing and considering the Transaction at the end of the second year) or the term of the contract, whichever is greater.
[83] b. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the parties' duty to hold in confidence Confidential Information that was disclosed during term shall remain in effect until the one hundred twentieth (120th) month after the date of this Agreement; provided, however, that the duty to hold in confidence any trade secrets and source code (including copyright application code) shall remain in effect for so long as such information remains a trade secret or source code under applicable law, and the expiry of the one hundred twentieth (120th) month shall not end or shorten that duty.
[84] 8. Remedies.
[85] a. The Parties acknowledge that the Confidential Information is of a unique and valuable character, and that the unauthorized dissemination of the Confidential Information could cause irreparable harm to the Party and the general public.
[86] b. Therefore, the Parties shall be entitled to injunctive relief preventing the dissemination of any Confidential Information in violation of the terms hereof.
[87] Such injunctive relief shall be in addition to any other remedies available hereunder, whether at law or in equity.
[88] c. The Discloser shall be entitled to recover its costs and fees, including reasonable attorneys' fees, incurred in obtaining any such relief or in recovering damages or other remedies for any breach of this Agreement.
[89] d. The Recipient shall be liable to the Discloser for all direct and consequential damages resulting from any breach of this Agreement by the Recipient or its Representatives, in addition to the relief described in paragraph 8b.
[90] The Recipient further acknowledges that the unauthorized disclosure of certain information pertaining to "Critical Assets" or "Critical Infrastructure" may constitute a violation of state and federal law.
[91] 9. Return of JEA Confidential Information.
[92] The Recipient shall immediately return and redeliver to the other all tangible material embodying the JEA Confidential Information provided hereunder and all notes, summaries, memoranda, drawings, manuals, records, excerpts or derivative information deriving there from and all other documents or materials ("Notes") (and all copies of any of the foregoing, including "copies" that have been converted to computerized media in the form of image, data or word processing files either manually or by image capture) based on or including any JEA Confidential Information, in whatever form of storage or retrieval, upon the earlier of -
[93] I. the completion or termination of the dealings between the parties contemplated hereunder; or
[94] II. the termination of this Agreement; or
[95] III. at such time as JEA may so request; provided however that the Recipient may retain only such of its documents as it is required by applicable law to retain, and any documents so retained remain subject to this Agreement.
[96] Alternatively, the Recipient, with the written consent of JEA, may immediately destroy any of the foregoing embodying JEA Confidential Information (or the reasonably non-recoverable data erasure of computerized data) and, upon request, certify in writing such destruction by an authorized officer of the Recipient supervising the destruction).
[97] JEA reserves the right to require evidence supporting such an activity.
[98] 10. Notice of Breach.
[99] The Recipient shall notify the Discloser immediately upon discovery that any Confidential Information has been communicated or distributed to any unauthorized person or entity and will cooperate with efforts by the Discloser to help the Discloser regain possession of Confidential Information and prevent its further unauthorized use.
[100] 11. No Warranty.
[101] The Discloser shall have no liability to the Recipient or the Representatives resulting from any use of the Confidential Information.
[102] The Discloser shall have sole responsibility for providing the Confidential Information necessary for Recipient to perform its obligations under the parties' Agreements.
[103] 12. Miscellaneous.
[104] a. This Agreement:
[105] i. is the complete agreement of the parties concerning the subject matter hereof and supersedes any prior such agreements with respect to further disclosures on such subject matter;
[106] ii. may not be amended or in any manner modified except in writing signed by the parties;
[107] iii. shall be governed and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware without regard to its conflict of law provisions; and
[108] iv. shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties and their respective successors, assigns and designees.
[109] b. The Federal and state courts located in Duval County, Florida shall have sole and exclusive jurisdiction over any disputes arising under this Agreement.
[110] If any provision of this Agreement is found to be unenforceable, the remainder shall be enforced as fully as possible and the unenforceable provision shall be deemed modified to the limited extent required to permit its enforcement in a manner most closely representing the intention of the parties as expressed herein.
[111] Any failure by the Discloser to enforce the strict performance of any provision of this Agreement will not constitute a waiver of its right to subsequently enforce such provision or any other provision of this Agreement.
[112] c. Any notices required or permitted to be given hereunder may be delivered by hand, deposited with a nationally recognized overnight carrier, electronic-mail, or mailed by certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, in each case, to the address of the other party first indicated above.
[113] All such notices or communications shall be deemed to have been given and received
[114] (a) in the case of personal delivery or electronic-mail, on the date of such delivery,
[115] (b) in the case of delivery by a nationally recognized overnight carrier, on the third business day following dispatch and
[116] (c) in the case of mailing, on the seventh business day following such mailing.
[117] IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties hereto have executed this Agreement as of the date first above written.
[118] JEA
[119] Recipient
[120] By
[121] __________________________
[122] By
[123] __________________________
[124] Name: Name:
